To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) plasma from CLL patients contain elevated levels of cell free DNA, which is associated with disease progression; 2) CLL cells with high TLR9 signaling promote disease progression and are more migratory and 3) dual targeting of TRL9 and BTK is strongly synergistic, highlighting the potential of TLR9 as a novel therapeutic target.
TLR9 is a potential novel therapeutic target in CLL and that combined targeting of BCR and TLR signaling pathways may improve treatment response.
TLR9 is a promising novel target for CLL treatment and that combined targeting of TRL9 and BTK is highly synergistic and could be a promising new treatment strategy.

the identification of new prognostic markers and novel therapeutic targets in CLL.
the role of TLR9 signaling and its impact on CLL cell biology and disease progression.
